pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented with specific reference to his own body — three to four sessions of 45 minutes, plus a daily 5-15 minute mobility routine 'specific to you, to those knees, the shoulders, the herniated disc that you have at the moment'. Asked the check, he answered 'Yes' and the rep noted 'Love the conviction'. Agreed without questions and without volunteering anything, which is notable given he had just described a 6-out-of-10 pain level in four joints — the pillar aimed directly at his problem and drew only a flat yes.

Framed around his actual constraint, eating on the road across rotating shifts — the what/when/how-much model, whole foods, no calorie counting, no chicken and rice. He responded with a commitment rather than a question: 'Yeah, I can stick to a protocol. I can actually work around that. I can make that work.' He had already diagnosed his own nutrition problem earlier (carbs, sandwiches, processed meats, hotels without kitchens), so the pillar was landing on ground he had prepared himself.

The pillar he bought. He named accountability as his gap before it was presented — 'I know what to do. I just have no accountability' — and when asked what would help most he came back to it unprompted: 'just accountability will be the main... it'll give me the drive'. He then elaborated with his own metaphor, quoting Rocky: 'there is no tomorrow. So today, with accountability, you have that process.' He also pre-enacted the mechanism, imagining Trevor's chasing message: 'oh, I'm going to get a nasty email, text message, or a phone call. Like, what are you doing?' Volunteered, tied to his own goal, and expressed in his own language.

anchors.raw: right now my work is kind of inconsistent, so... because all this war stuff and not getting parts and stuff, you know, telecommunications and that, you know, I roughly have about $1,500 a month
anchors.note: The controlling anchor, and a different shape from ordinary affordability. He is not poor and not unwilling — he has $2,500 liquid and a $1,500 monthly surplus — but he does not know whether next month exists. The current assignment might end the same night. Against that, a fixed six-month commitment is a risk rather than a cost.

anchors.raw: Out of my four credit cards right now, I have almost $3,000 in debt, so I just want to try and get those paid off too.
anchors.note: He has a competing financial project he is emotionally committed to — paying down cards and rebuilding a poor credit score. The rep handled this well, explicitly declining to route the purchase through credit: 'I'm not saying we should put on credit and use a loan or anything.' Ethically right, and it also removed the only large lever available.

anchors.raw: my doctor said, you know, I'll give you six months to get it together, or we'll just put you on a fitness program... blood pressure medicine, things that I don't want to do
anchors.note: The strongest supportive anchor in the batch. A named authority has set a real six-month clock with a consequence he has spent years avoiding, reinforced by his father's advice never to start blood pressure medication. He also has a doctor's appointment at the end of August he wants to walk into having already started. The rep touched this twice but never made it the close, which is the biggest missed lever on the call.

anchors.raw: I'm paying for all these applications to stream TV so I can watch TV, and that's why I haven't been working out, so if I'm more working out, I'm not watching TV, so I can get rid of these, you know, extra things that I, that's keeping me lazy.
anchors.competitor: streaming subscriptions and other recurring memberships
anchors.note: He built his own funding plan out loud, and better still, framed the thing being cancelled as a cause of the problem. This is a prospect selling himself. The rep reinforced it correctly. Worth capturing as a reusable pattern — asking a travelling prospect what recurring spend keeps them sedentary.

anchors.raw: I always have a hotel that has a fitness center, but, you know, sometimes they don't have what you want in there. They just might have a treadmill.
anchors.competitor: hotel gyms and self-directed travel workouts
anchors.note: A weak substitute and he knows it — he raised it and immediately explained why it fails, then described shipping his own kettlebells to job sites. This anchor works in the offer's favour and needed no handling.

anchors.raw: not like this quick 28-day stuff that everyone's advertising, military fitness, stuff like that
anchors.note: The category he has been shopping is cheap, short and mass-market. He is explicitly rejecting it on substance, which helps, but it means his reference price for online fitness is set by products that sell for tens of dollars, not thousands. No pre-framing of the price had happened before this call.

unmet_demand.want: A payment structure that can absorb a month with no work — pausing, deferring or flexing an instalment when an assignment ends early
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only flexibility offered was splitting into six fixed monthly payments, which converts an affordability problem into a recurring obligation against an income he cannot forecast. He said plainly that if the assignment ends he will be 'dipping into my 1500 bucks to pay for things that I normally get when I'm traveling'. Nothing in the offer handles irregular income.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that loaded kettlebell training is safe with a herniated disc
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He disclosed the herniated disc plainly and the response folded it into the sales pitch — a daily mobility routine 'specific to you, to those knees, the shoulders, the herniated disc... to make sure it's only going to make it better'. That is a therapeutic claim about a spinal condition, made without any clinical qualification, in a programme built on loaded hip hinges. Nobody asked whether his doctor has cleared him for resistance training, and he is currently under active medical supervision.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that adapts to rotating shift work — training and eating across alternating midnight and day weeks
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted this would be handled ('when are you traveling, with your nighttime shifts as well, to just make it all workable') but nothing concrete was described, and shift rotation is a harder problem than travel — it disrupts sleep, appetite and recovery on a fortnightly cycle. Plausibly served by a coach who plans around your life; never actually evidenced.

unmet_demand.want: Preparation specifically for Spartan obstacle course racing at short notice
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was his opening statement of what he wants and it was folded into a generic athletic-build benefit, then used once as a closing image. Nobody established whether kettlebell training plus mobility actually prepares someone for obstacle racing, or whether the programme would build toward an event. Likely defensible, entirely unaddressed.
